clue.text: Fish that can fasten without a painful expression?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the fastening word wraps round the cry

parts.note: to seal something is to fasten it shut
ow is the cry of someone hurt

explanation.surface: A riddle about a fish that can close things up without wincing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. The sea owl is another name for the lumpsucker.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea owl is a name for the lumpsucker, a North Atlantic fish.

clue.text: Separate if in the way

indicators.note: in places the little word inside the abbreviation for a road

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestion to keep things apart whenever they obstruct you.
explanation.definitionFit: To sift is to separate fine material from coarse, as with a sieve.

clue.text: Star worker to sign one out

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

indicators.note: out tells us the numeral-like letter is dropped from the zodiac sign

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A star employee signs someone out of the building.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking I out of ARIES leaves ARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is the bright red star in the constellation Scorpius.

clue.text: Learned area of person affecting knowledge

parts.note: learned means wise
an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: A scholarly field belonging to someone who influences what is known.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a know-all who pretends to wisdom, a person feigning knowledge.

clue.text: Bad marks for parts on style

definitions.meaning: stigmas in the sense of signs of disgrace, with the classical plural
in a flower the stigma is the tip sitting on top of the style, the stalk of the pistil

explanation.surface: Poor grades handed out for parts of a fashion show.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of stigma, a mark of disgrace, and also the pollen-receiving tips atop a flower's styles.

clue.text: Heavenly strike almost gets the lower pin

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: under means lower, below
a bolt is a metal pin that fastens

explanation.surface: A bowling strike that nearly takes out the bottom pin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightning flash with its crash of thunder, a strike from the heavens.

clue.text: Group contains one prodigy

indicators.note: contains places the numeral inside the classification word

parts.note: a genus is a biological group
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A band includes one musical wunderkind.
explanation.definitionFit: A genius is an exceptionally gifted person, a synonym for a prodigy.

clue.text: I am turning up with one peg, perhaps

definitions.text: I am turning up with one peg, perhaps

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turning says the little word next to it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
a golf tee is a small peg

explanation.surface: Someone announces their arrival on a single wooden leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes PU from UP. The whole clue also describes the speaker, someone with one peg leg.
explanation.definitionFit: An amputee has lost a limb, and might walk on a single wooden peg leg.

clue.text: Switch C and B in box?

definitions.meaning: to switch is to change over, take turns
Cox and Box are the two lodgers in the farce Box and Cox, who use the same room by turns, one by day, one by night

explanation.surface: Instructions to swap two letters inside a container.
explanation.walkthrough: Box and Cox is a Victorian English farce (later a Sullivan operetta) whose title became a byword for taking turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternate means to change over by turns, which is what the two farce lodgers do with their room.

clue.text: Angle covering alien fixation

indicators.note: covering puts the fishing word round the extraterrestrial

parts.note: to angle is to fish
ET is the film's extraterrestrial, an alien

explanation.surface: An obsession with how one approaches extraterrestrials.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an obsessive fixation on some object or activity.

clue.text: Roaster does so to get tip

definitions.text: Roaster does so to get tip

parts.words: Roaster does so to get tip
parts.note: a kitchen boy roasting meat turns the spit, hoping for a tip; and turning the letters of spit round gives tips

explanation.surface: A cook rotates the meat in hope of a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnspit was a servant, or dog, employed to turn a roasting spit by hand.

clue.text: Routine to study and speak when beheaded, so to speak

parts.note: read 'so to speak' as B-headed: each word gets a B at its head
to read is to study
the same B-heading applied to the second word
to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: Reading up and talking after decapitation is a strange daily routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' normally means losing a first letter; 'so to speak' says read it as B-headed, so B is added to the front of READ and of UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread-and-butter work is the basic, routine everyday business that provides a living.

clue.text: Islands are around bit on leaving bay

indicators.note: around says the first word wraps the small piece

parts.note: taken as written
a chip is a small bit

indicators.note: leaving says the little word departs from the larger one

parts.note: a lagoon is a sheltered bay of water
taken as written

explanation.surface: Isles lie round a small piece once you exit the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: LAGOON with ON leaving gives LAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: An archipelago is a group or chain of islands.

clue.text: Dagger gives room for breaking the rules

definitions.meaning: a thin medieval dagger used for the mercy stroke
the room in a monastery where monks could relax the rule, eating meat for example

explanation.surface: A weapon provides space for rule-breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the Latin for mercy: a mercy-stroke dagger and a monastic room of indulgence.

clue.text: Expedient to run up loose dress

parts.note: to run up a garment is to make it quickly
a shift is a loose straight dress

explanation.surface: A handy fix: sew yourself a simple frock.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift is a temporary expedient, something used for want of better.

clue.text: Consume salmon cutlet at high table

indicators.note: read as cut-let, a small cut taken out of the words consume salmon

explanation.surface: Diners eat salmon cutlets at the top table.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across consuME SAlmon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesa is a flat-topped hill with steep sides, a natural high tableland.

clue.text: Eve shows little will in drunken state

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the drink word

parts.note: tight means drunk

indicators.note: little means the word is cut short by a letter

explanation.surface: Eve reveals her faint resolve while tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little will' is WILL with its last letter dropped, WIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve in its sense of evening, so the dusk of twilight.

clue.text: Recoil can lead off, start, turn and back

definitions.meaning: the ... of a gun is its recoil

definitions.text: can lead off, start, turn and back
definitions.meaning: the word goes before each to make ...-off, ...-start, ...-turn and kickback

explanation.surface: A gun's recoil can trigger a whole chain of movements.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm's kick is the backward jolt it gives when fired.

clue.text: Preserve grim sincerity

parts.note: to can fruit is to preserve it
dour means grim, stern

explanation.surface: Jam-making with a stern, honest face.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour is frankness and openness, close in meaning to sincerity.

clue.text: Mammal's wail to help at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A creature's cry for assistance out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilot whale is a large dolphin, a marine mammal.

clue.text: Planes ran features backing magazine

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
features says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Aircraft carried articles supporting a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store of weapons and ammunition, which is one sense of magazine.

clue.text: Mineral (barium) taken from church

indicators.note: taken from says the element symbol is removed from the building word

parts.note: a basilica is a type of church
Ba is the chemical symbol for barium

explanation.surface: A mineral, barium, has been removed from a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Silica is silicon dioxide, the mineral found as quartz and sand.

clue.text: In logic, it turns one mad first to indulge in fanciful emotion

indicators.note: In at the front says everything that follows goes inside the logic word

parts.note: sense means logic, reasonableness

indicators.note: first says the word for mad comes before the numeral
turns says the two-letter word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
mental is slang for mad
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Within reasoning, someone crazy becomes overly emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the very start signals the container: the whole run that follows sits inside the word for logic, and 'turns' makes the reversed IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To sentimentalise is to indulge in sentiment, treating things with mawkish emotion.

clue.text: The thread of the story

definitions.meaning: spun fibre for knitting or weaving
a tale, often a tall one

explanation.surface: Through-line of the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarn is both spun thread and an informal word for a long story.

clue.text: Wry one to gloss over and press ahead

indicators.note: ahead says the pressing word goes in front

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: over says the gloss word is turned backwards

parts.note: lac is a resin used for glossy lacquer

explanation.surface: A dry type tries to smooth things over and push on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns LAC into CAL; 'ahead' brings IRON to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironical means wryly mocking, saying the opposite of what is meant.

clue.text: Programme concerning time and motion

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: motion means movement, so the letters of the little word are stirred

explanation.surface: Schedule involving a time-and-motion study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerning' is a link; 'motion' rearranges AND into NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a programme of items to be dealt with at a meeting.

clue.text: Rider who could return straddled over a bull?

definitions.text: Rider who could return straddled over a bull?

parts.words: Rider who could return straddled over a bull?
parts.note: a mounted bullfighter who, if things went badly, might come back slung across the animal

explanation.surface: A horseman might come home draped over a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador is a bullfighter, originally one who fought on horseback.

clue.text: Wrap neck first when hot

parts.note: a stole is a wrap worn round the shoulders

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of neck

explanation.surface: Wrap your neck first when the weather is warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen, as in hot goods.
